$comment: The company-registration status this codebase PUBLISHES A CLAIM ABOUT.
web/app/mentions-legales/page.tsx tells the public, in French, that MyWeli is
« société en cours d'immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et du Crédit
Mobilier de Côte d'Ivoire ». That is a representation to users, to salons and
to the app stores. It is TRUE as of the date below (owner-confirmed), and it
is the kind of statement that stops being true without anything in this repo
changing.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until 2026-08-22 the only automated thing touching the
claim was web/tests/legal.test.tsx, which asserted the claim was STILL
PENDING — so it went red the day someone CORRECTED it and stayed green
forever while it rotted. A guard pointed at the wrong end of the fact.
AND THE 'ONE EDIT' WAS NEVER TRUE. lib/legal.ts and mentions-legales/page.tsx
both claimed COMPANY was the single edit that completes registration. The
claim has every surface listed below — most of them hard-coded prose, across
three different documents. NO COUNT IS WRITTEN IN THIS PROSE, deliberately:
the array is the count, and a number beside a list is a second source of
truth that only ever goes stale. The first version of this file said FIVE
while the array held SEVEN. Editing the constant alone leaves the mentions
légales contradicting themselves one paragraph later, and leaves the privacy
policy promising a future event that has already happened.
Read in two directions, like infra/gcp/logging-manifest.json:
web/tests/registration-claim.test.ts   manifest <-> every listed surface
(offline, merge gate, CLOCK-FREE)
infra/legal/98-verify-registration-attestation.mjs
attestedOn <-> today
(the daily monitor, never a gate)
WHY THE STALENESS HALF IS NOT A UNIT TEST. web/tests/stub-clock.test.ts says
it best: « a suite that is green at every hour except one fails a future PR
at random and looks like that PR's fault. » Web unit tests block merges. So
consistency is asserted in the gate (no clock), and staleness is asserted on
the production-checks cron, which opens an issue and cannot block anyone.
WHAT TO DO WHEN THE ISSUE OPENS. Either the company is now registered — flip
`registered` to true, and the test will fail listing EVERY surface still
carrying pending prose until each is rewritten — or it is not, and you bump
`attestedOn` to today. Both are one-line edits reviewed in a PR. The point is
that re-confirming is cheap and forgetting is noisy.
THE SCAN IS THE PART THAT DEFENDS ITSELF. Listing surfaces by hand fixes those
instances; it does not fix the blindness. `scan` re-derives the surface list
from the source tree on every run, so a NEW sentence written next month
fails until it is recorded here. Comments are stripped before matching —
four separate guards in this repo have matched text that lived only in a
comment, one of them the comment explaining that very footgun.
IT EARNED ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN. The surface list below was hand-built
from a careful case-insensitive grep, reviewed, and still missed one of
the two lines of the mentions-légales Callout. The scan found that one; a
later audit of the same step found another, in a design doc. A list built
by reading is always shorter than the tree — which is the whole argument
for deriving it rather than maintaining it.
attestedBy: owner, in conversation — « for now the company is not registered »

surfaces.what: COMPANY.registration — the sentence the mentions légales renders
surfaces.atRegistration: replace with the RCCM number and the registered name

surfaces.what: COMPANY.pendingFacts — the five facts the page says are missing
surfaces.atRegistration: empty the list and publish the facts themselves

surfaces.what: the Callout — hard-coded, NOT read from COMPANY
the Callout's second sentence — the promise to publish later
Directeur de la publication defers to a section that will be gone
the L1 spec: §9 scope and the Annex A.4 source copy
surfaces.atRegistration: update §9 and Annex A.4 to the published RCCM facts

surfaces.what: the SMS/WhatsApp section conditions Termii on this same event
surfaces.atRegistration: restate as a present-tense fact, whichever way it lands

$comment: Every line under `roots` matching `pattern`, after comments are stripped,
must contain one of the surface anchors above or one of the exemptions
below. Exemptions are by MEANING, not by line number: both inline hits are
about the registration papers a SALON uploads, which is a different
subject, and lib/pro/kyc.ts is that subject's whole module.
$roots_comment: web/ SOURCE ONLY, deliberately. The scan's job is the sentences a
visitor can read; widening it to docs/ would flag every paragraph that
discusses registration and be switched off within a month. The one doc
that must change at registration — this spec's Annex A.4 — is a recorded
surface above instead, which is the narrow claim the scan cannot make.
It uses a STRAIGHT apostrophe where the code uses U+2019; anchors are
matched byte-for-byte, so the two are not interchangeable.
AT REGISTRATION, ONE STEP THE SCAN CANNOT INFER. The replacement wording
— « immatriculée au RCCM n° ... » — matches `pattern` too, so the scan will
demand it be recorded. It must NOT become a surface: a surface's anchor has
to be ABSENT once registered, and this one is the thing being published.
